verdict: Comfort Systems had a blowout quarter: revenue rose 54% to $3.77B and profit rose 68% to $489M as construction demand — much of it data centers — pushed backlog to a record $17.8B.

segments.name: Mechanical
segments.note: Heating, ventilation, air-conditioning and plumbing construction and services — 69% of revenue (segment detail from the company's 10-Q).

segments.name: Electrical
segments.note: Electrical construction and services — up 85% as data-center and industrial projects surged (segment detail from the company's 10-Q).

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: SG&A of $314.2M, partly offset by a $4.3M gain on the sale of assets — shown net so the chart foots to reported operating income.

otherDetail: Interest income, net of $14.5M, less a $4.3M increase in the fair value of earn-out obligations owed on past acquisitions, plus $0.3M of other income.

takeaways.title: Growth most builders never see
takeaways.text: Revenue grew 54% year over year — technology customers alone were 61% of revenue, reflecting the data-center construction boom — and gross margin held at 24.8% despite the pace.

takeaways.title: Backlog nearly doubled
takeaways.text: Backlog reached $17.81B, up from $9.38B a year ago and $14.06B just last quarter — about $3.8B of new work added in three months, most of it same-store rather than acquired.

takeaways.title: Cash followed the profit
takeaways.text: Operating cash flow was $1.01B in the quarter — more than double net income — as customers paid advances on the swelling project pipeline.
